def-null-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold:
## Definition

Let $M$ be a smooth $m$-manifold, and let $\mathcal A$ be a smooth atlas on
$M$. A subset $A\subseteq M$ is **$\mathcal A$-null** when, for every chart
$(U,\varphi)\in\mathcal A$, the set

$$\varphi(A\cap U)\subseteq\mathbb R^m$$

is null in the Euclidean sense of [[def-null-and-content-zero-in-rn]] when
$m\ge 1$, and is empty when $m=0$. Equivalently, on a $0$-manifold the only
null subset is the empty set.

Under the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the next proposition shows that this
condition is independent of the chosen smooth atlas. Under that premise one
may therefore speak simply of a **null subset of $M$**.
lem-a-c1-map-is-locally-lipschitz-on-com:
## Statement

Let $F:M\to N$ be $C^1$, let $(U,\varphi)$ be a chart on $M$, let $(V,\psi)$ be
a chart on $N$ with $F(U)\subseteq V$, and let $K\subseteq U$ be compact. Then
every point of $K$ has an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq U$ with
$\overline W\subseteq U$ such that the coordinate representative
$\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}$ is Lipschitz on $\varphi(\overline W)$.
lem-c1-local-diffeomorphisms-preserve-nu:
## Statement

Let $F:M\to N$ be a $C^1$ local diffeomorphism. For every $p\in M$
there are coordinate neighbourhoods $(U,\varphi)$ of $p$ and
$(V,\psi)$ of $F(p)$ such that $F|_U:U\to V$ is a diffeomorphism and,
for every $A\subseteq U$, using the closed-cube nullity of [[def-null-and-content-zero-in-rn]],

$$\varphi(A)\text{ is null in }\mathbb R^n \iff \psi(F(A))\text{ is null in }\mathbb R^n.$$

For $n=0$, “null” means empty.
prop-the-null-set-definition-is-independ:
## Statement

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ are smooth atlases on the same smooth manifold
$M$, then a subset $E\subseteq M$ is $\mathcal A$-null if and only if it is
$\mathcal B$-null.
prop-a-countable-chart-cover-detects-man:
## Statement

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold. If $\{(U_j,\varphi_j)\}_{j\in\mathbb N}$ is a
countable smooth atlas with relatively compact domains, then a subset
$E\subseteq M$ is null if and only if every $\varphi_j(E\cap U_j)$ is null in
$\mathbb R^{\dim M}$ when $\dim M\ge 1$, and every
$\varphi_j(E\cap U_j)$ is empty when $\dim M=0$.
prop-countable-unions-and-subsets-of-man:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every subset of a manifold null set is
null, and every countable union of manifold null sets is null.
prop-a-null-set-has-dense-complement-in-:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a positive-dimensional smooth manifold, let $\mathcal A$ be a smooth
atlas on $M$, and let $E\subseteq M$ be $\mathcal A$-null in the sense of
[[def-null-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold]]. Then $M\setminus E$ is dense in $M$.
In particular, under Countable Choice the conclusion holds for any manifold-null
set $E$.
prop-an-equidimensional-c1-map-sends-nul:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $F:M^m\to N^m$ be a $C^1$ map between smooth manifolds of the same
dimension. If $E\subseteq M$ is null, then $F(E)\subseteq N$ is null.
prop-the-image-of-a-lower-dimensional-c1:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $P^m$ and $N^n$ be smooth manifolds with $m<n$, and let $F:P\to N$ be a
$C^1$ map. Then $F(P)\subseteq N$ is a null subset of $N$.
cor-positive-codimension-immersed-subman:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every immersed submanifold of positive codimension in a smooth manifold is a
null subset of the ambient manifold.
def-c1-critical-locus-and-critical-value:
## Definition

Let $m\ge0$ and $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let
$F\in C^1(U,\mathbb R^n)$. Here $C^1$ has the componentwise Euclidean
meaning of [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]. For each
$x\in U$, $DF_x$ is the total derivative: the linear map $L$ satisfying
$F(x+h)=F(x)+Lh+o(\|h\|_2)$ as in
[[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]]. The **$C^1$ critical locus** of
$F$ is

$$
\operatorname{Crit}_{C^1}(F):=\{x\in U:DF_x(\mathbb R^m)\ne\mathbb R^n\}.
$$

The **$C^1$ critical-value set** is

$$
\operatorname{CV}_{C^1}(F):=F(\operatorname{Crit}_{C^1}(F)).
$$

A value outside this set is a regular value; in particular, a value with empty
fibre is regular. This definition uses only the first derivative, so it applies
to $C^1$ maps that need not be smooth.

When $m=0$, the only open domains are $\varnothing$ and $\{0\}$. On
$\varnothing$ both sets are empty. On $\{0\}$, the unique total derivative
$\mathbb R^0\to\mathbb R^n$ is zero and is not onto because $n\ge1$, so the
domain point is critical and its image is the critical-value set.
def-critical-locus-and-critical-value-se:
## Definition

Let $F:M\to N$ be smooth. The **critical locus** of $F$ is

$$\operatorname{Crit}(F):=\{p\in M:p\text{ is a critical point of }F\},$$

and the **critical value set** of $F$ is its image

$$\operatorname{CV}(F):=F(\operatorname{Crit}(F)).$$

Its complement $N\setminus\operatorname{CV}(F)$ is the set of regular values.
lem-sard-slicing-for-compact-null-sectio:
## Statement

Let $n\ge 1$, let $a\le b$, and let $K\subseteq [a,b]\times\mathbb R^n$ be compact. For each
$t\in[a,b]$, write

$$ K_t:=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:(t,y)\in K\}. $$

If every section $K_t$ is a null subset of $\mathbb R^n$, then $K$ is a null
subset of $\mathbb R^{n+1}$.
thm-whitney-extension-for-finite-order-e:
## Statement

Let $d,N\ge1$, let $A$ be a closed subset of $\mathbb R^d$, $r$ a nonnegative integer,
and, for each $a\in A$, let $P_a$ be a polynomial of degree at most $r$
with values in $\mathbb R^N$. Suppose that on each compact part of $A$,
for every multi-index $|\alpha|\le r$,
$$D^\alpha P_a(b)-D^\alpha P_b(b)=o(|a-b|^{r-|\alpha|})\quad(a,b\in A,\ |a-b|\to0)$$
uniformly in $a,b$. Then there is a $C^r$ map
$H:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^N$ whose order-$r$ Taylor polynomial at
each $a\in A$ is $P_a$. The construction needs no choice axiom.
lem-kneser-glaeser-rough-composition-on-:
## Statement

Let $0\le s<r$ be integers, $V\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ and
$W\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ open, $A\subseteq V$, and $A^*\subseteq W$
closed relative to $W$. Let $f:V\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^r$ with
$D^jf=0$ on $A$ for $1\le j\le s$, and let $g:W\to V$ be
$C^{r-s}$ with $g(A^*)\subseteq A$. Then there is a $C^r$ map
$H:W\to\mathbb R^n$ such that $H=f\circ g$ on $A^*$ and
$D^jH=0$ on $A^*$ for $1\le j\le s$.
lem-sard-on-the-nonflat-critical-strata:
## Statement

Let $m,n\ge 1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^r$, and for $j\ge 1$ define

$$ C_j:=\{x\in U:D^\alpha f(x)=0\text{ for every multi-index }1\le |\alpha|\le j\}. $$

If $1\le j<r$, $K\subseteq C_j\setminus C_{j+1}$ is compact, and the
Morse-Sard conclusion is already known for $C^r$ maps from open subsets of
$\mathbb R^{m-1}$ to $\mathbb R^n$, then $f(K)$ is null.
lem-sard-on-the-infinitely-flat-critical:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$ and $r\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^r$ with
$rn\ge m$. Let

$$ C_r:=\{x\in U:D^\alpha f(x)=0\text{ for every multi-index }1\le |\alpha|\le r\}. $$

If $K\subseteq C_r$ is compact, then $f(K)$ is null in $\mathbb R^n$.
thm-morse-sard-for-euclidean-maps:
## Statement

Let $m\ge0$, $n\ge1$, and $r\ge1$ be integers, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be a $C^r$ map with

$$ r>\max\{m-n,0\}. $$

Then the critical value set of $f$ is a null subset of $\mathbb R^n$.
thm-morse-sard-for-smooth-manifolds:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $F:M\to N$ be a smooth map between smooth manifolds. Then the critical value
set of $F$ is a null subset of $N$.
cor-regular-values-have-null-complement-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For a smooth map $F:M\to N$, the complement of the regular values is a null
subset of $N$. In particular, the regular values are dense in $N$.
prop-the-critical-value-set-of-a-smooth-:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). For a smooth map
$F:M\to N$, the critical value set $\operatorname{CV}(F)$ is a
$\sigma$-compact subset of $N$.
cor-regular-values-form-a-dense-g-delta-:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). For a smooth map
$F:M\to N$, the set of regular values is a dense
$G_\delta$ subset of $N$.
cor-a-smooth-map-from-lower-to-higher-di:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $F:M^m\to N^n$ is smooth and $m<n$, then $F$ is not surjective onto any
nonempty $N$.
def-transverse-linear-subspaces:
## Definition

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let $A,B\le V$ be linear
subspaces. They are **transverse**, written $A\pitchfork B$, when

$$A+B=V.$$

Equivalently,

$$\dim(A\cap B)=\dim A+\dim B-\dim V$$

by [[thm-dimension-formula]].
def-a-smooth-map-transverse-to-an-embedd:
## Definition

Let $F:M\to N$ be smooth, and let $Z\subseteq N$ be an embedded submanifold.
Then $F$ is **transverse to $Z$**, written $F\pitchfork Z$, when for every
$p\in F^{-1}(Z)$,

$$dF_p(T_pM)+T_{F(p)}Z=T_{F(p)}N.$$

If $F(M)\cap Z=\varnothing$, this condition is vacuous, so $F\pitchfork Z$
still holds.
def-transverse-smooth-maps:
## Definition

Let $F:M\to N$ and $G:P\to N$ be smooth maps. They are **transverse**, written
$F\pitchfork G$, when for every pair $(p,q)\in M\times P$ with
$F(p)=G(q)=y$,

$$dF_p(T_pM)+dG_q(T_qP)=T_yN.$$
def-transverse-embedded-submanifolds:
## Definition

Let $S,T\subseteq M$ be embedded submanifolds. They are **transverse**, written
$S\pitchfork T$, when their inclusion maps into $M$ are transverse. Equivalently,
for every $p\in S\cap T$,

$$T_pS+T_pT=T_pM.$$
lem-transversality-is-equivalent-to-surj:
## Statement

Let $F:M\to N$ be smooth, let $Z\subseteq N$ be an embedded submanifold, and let
$p\in F^{-1}(Z)$ with $y=F(p)$. Then $F$ is transverse to $Z$ at $p$ if and
only if the composite

$$ T_pM\xrightarrow{dF_p}T_yN\twoheadrightarrow T_yN/T_yZ $$

is surjective.
thm-transverse-preimage-theorem:
## Statement

Let $F:M^m\to N^n$ be smooth and let $Z\subseteq N$ be an embedded submanifold
of codimension $c$. If $F\pitchfork Z$, then $F^{-1}(Z)$ is an embedded
submanifold of $M$ of codimension $c$. For each $p\in F^{-1}(Z)$,

$$ T_pF^{-1}(Z)=\{v\in T_pM:dF_p(v)\in T_{F(p)}Z\}. $$
cor-transverse-intersection-theorem:
## Statement

If $S,T\subseteq M$ are transverse embedded submanifolds of codimensions $a$ and
$b$, then $S\cap T$ is an embedded submanifold of codimension $a+b$. At each
$p\in S\cap T$,

$$ T_p(S\cap T)=T_pS\cap T_pT. $$
thm-transverse-fibre-product-theorem:
## Statement

Let $F:M\to N$ and $G:P\to N$ be smooth and transverse. Then the fibre product

$$ M\times_N P:=\{(p,q)\in M\times P:F(p)=G(q)\} $$

is an embedded submanifold of $M\times P$.
cor-a-submersion-is-transverse-to-every-:
## Statement

If $F:M\to N$ is a submersion, then $F\pitchfork Z$ for every embedded
submanifold $Z\subseteq N$.
prop-transversality-to-a-point-is-the-re:
## Statement

For a smooth map $F:M\to N$ and a point $q\in N$, the condition $F\pitchfork\{q\}$
is equivalent to saying that $q$ is a regular value of $F$.
prop-transversality-is-invariant-under-d:
## Statement

Let $\Phi:M'\to M$ and $\Psi:N\to N'$ be diffeomorphisms.

1. If $F:M\to N$ and $G:P\to N$ are transverse, then
   $\Psi\circ F\circ\Phi$ and $\Psi\circ G$ are transverse.
2. If $Z\subseteq N$ is an embedded submanifold and $F\pitchfork Z$, then
   $\Psi\circ F\circ\Phi\pitchfork \Psi(Z)$.
prop-local-graph-characterization-by-tra:
## Statement

Let $S\subseteq M\times N$ be an embedded submanifold with $\dim S=\dim M$, and
let $(x_0,y_0)\in S$. If $S$ is transverse at $(x_0,y_0)$ to the vertical
fibre $\{x_0\}\times N$, then there exist neighbourhoods $U\subseteq M$ of
$x_0$ and $V\subseteq N$ of $y_0$ and a smooth map $f:U\to V$ such that

$$ S\cap(U\times V)=\{(x,f(x)):x\in U\}. $$
prop-global-graph-characterization-by-on:
## Statement

Let $S\subseteq M\times N$ be an embedded submanifold. Assume:

1. for every $x\in M$, the vertical fibre $\{x\}\times N$ meets $S$ in exactly
   one point; and
2. $S$ is transverse to every vertical fibre it meets.

Then there is a unique smooth map $f:M\to N$ with $S=\Gamma_f$.
def-smooth-family-of-maps-and-evaluation:
## Definition

Let $M$, $S$, and $N$ be smooth manifolds. A **smooth family of maps from $M$
to $N$ parametrized by $S$** is a smooth map

$$\mathcal F:M\times S\to N.$$

For each $s\in S$, its **slice map** is

$$\mathcal F_s:M\to N,\qquad \mathcal F_s(p):=\mathcal F(p,s).$$

The map $\mathcal F$ itself is the **evaluation map** of the family.
thm-parametric-transversality:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.
cor-generic-translations-of-a-map-to-euc:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $f:M\to\mathbb R^n$ be smooth and let $Z\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be an embedded
submanifold. Then the set of $a\in\mathbb R^n$ for which the translated map

$$ f_a(p):=f(p)+a $$

fails to be transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $\mathbb R^n$.
cor-outside-a-null-set-every-point-is-a-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $f:M\to\mathbb R^n$ be smooth and let $q\in\mathbb R^n$. Then outside a
null subset of $a\in\mathbb R^n$, the map $p\mapsto f(p)+a$ has $q$ as a regular
value.
prop-transversality-is-stable-on-a-compa:
## Statement

Let $M$ be compact, let $Z\subseteq N$ be a closed embedded submanifold, and let
$F:M\to N$ be smooth with $F\pitchfork Z$. Then every smooth map $G:M\to N$
sufficiently close to $F$ in the $C^1$ topology is also transverse to $Z$.
fs-every-critical-point-is-an-isolated-p:
## Statement

**False claim:** every critical point of a smooth map is isolated.
fs-the-set-of-critical-values-is-always-:
## Statement

**False claim:** the critical value set of a smooth map is always closed.
lem-a-c1-map-from-r2-to-r-with-an-interv:
## Statement

There is a map $F\in C^1(\mathbb R^2,\mathbb R)$ whose $C^1$ critical-value
set contains the interval $[0,2]$. In particular, that critical-value set is
not Euclidean null.
fs-sard-theorem-holds-for-every-c1-map-b:
## Statement

**False claim:** Sard's theorem remains true for every $C^1$ map between
arbitrary dimensions.

The differentiability threshold in [[thm-morse-sard-for-euclidean-maps]] is
real: the locally proved Cantor-sum construction below gives a $C^1$ map
$\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ whose critical values contain $[0,2]$.
fs-two-submanifolds-with-nonempty-inters:
## Statement

**False claim:** any two embedded submanifolds with nonempty intersection are
transverse.
fs-the-preimage-of-every-embedded-subman:
## Statement

**False claim:** the preimage of every embedded submanifold under a smooth map is
again a submanifold.
fs-transversality-is-globally-open-for-a:
## Statement

**False claim:** if $M$ is noncompact and $F:M\to N$ is transverse to an
embedded submanifold $Z\subseteq N$, then every map uniformly $C^1$-close to
$F$ is still transverse to $Z$.
